author: Robert Tait in Washington
description:
President says deal essential to lower US fuel prices but move set to create fresh crisis with Ukraine and Nato allies

  • US politics – live updates

Donald Trump was on a fresh collision course with the Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, and European allies on Friday after a stunning agreement to buy Russian diesel, upending years of US and western pressure on the Kremlin to end its four-and-a-half year war against Ukraine.

Zelenskyy reacted furiously to Trump’s announcement of the deal with President Vladimir Putin of Russia, calling it “absolutely t
title: Zelenskyy furious as Trump announces deal to buy Russian diesel

author: Richard Adams Education editor
description:
Unions tell government to fix ‘overbearing mess’ of inspection regime and its impact on staff wellbeing – or risk industrial action

Tensions between England’s headteachers and Ofsted are developing into a crisis after school leadership unions said they had no confidence in the watchdog and would hold strike ballots unless “significant wellbeing issues” caused by Ofsted’s inspections regime were fixed.

The Association of School and College Leaders​ (ASCL), which includes senior leaders in many secondary schools, described Ofsted’s inspection system as “an overbearing mess” and urged the government to pause inspections to stop teachers leaving the profession.

Continue reading...
title: Headteachers threaten strike ballots after losing confidence in Ofsted

author: Tess Ikonomou
description:
With GLP-1s to treat the condition not specifically approved by the TGA, patients are being prescribed them off-label

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Women living with a chronic hormonal condition should have access to taxpayer-funded weight loss medications, advocates say.

The Polyendrocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome Association of Australia (POSAA) is urging for GLP-1 drugs to be approved on the Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme for people living with the condition.

Continue reading...
title: Women with PMOS should get subsidised weight loss drugs, advocates say

author: Marina Dunbar
description:
Motorist, reportedly trying to beat a traffic light, barrels through busy intersection and slams into pedestrians

At least one person was killed and nine injured in New York City’s eastern Bronx when a motorist barreled through a busy intersection, slammed into pedestrians and triggered a chain-reaction crash involving several vehicles, according to authorities and media reports.

The horrifying collision happened shortly after 2pm in the Bronx’s Allerton neighborhood, with the driver at the center of the crash reportedly saying he was trying to beat a traffic light.

Continue reading...
title: One person killed and nine injured in chain-reaction crash in New York City

author: Agence France-Press
description:
Australian brothers Jake and Callum Robinson, 30 and 33, and friend Carter Rhoad, 30, were killed on a surfing trip in 2024

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A Mexican judge has convicted three men of the 2024 murders of two Australian surfers and their American friend in a case that sparked international outrage.

Australian brothers Jake and Callum Robinson, aged 30 and 33 respectively, and their friend Carter Rhoad, 30, were on a surfing trip to Mexico’s Pacific coast when they were shot dead in Baja California state in a suspected robbery.

Continue reading...
title: Three men found guilty of murders of Australian surfer brothers and US friend in Mexico

author: Ramon Antonio Vargas
description:
Actor was robbed of his watch after being struck in the head by two attackers wielding a gun and a knife

The Pretty Little Liars actor Keegan Allen was battered and robbed by attackers wielding a knife and gun in West Hollywood, he said on Thursday in a social media video showing him bloodied and alarmed.

The Los Angeles county sheriff’s department confirmed in a statement shared with news outlets that it was investigating a violent robbery matching the weapons, block and time described by Allen on social media, where users responded with shock and supportive comments.

Continue reading...
title: Pretty Little Liars’ Keegan Allen attacked by masked assailants in LA

author: Auzzy Byrdsell in New York
description:
Locals also express fear after man shot in the neck while his child was in the back of his car

Residents of Manhattan’s Marble Hill neighborhood were furious at federal Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) on Friday but also scared after an officer shot their neighbor who had his child in the back of his car.

Orlando Perez had parked his car on the corner of 225th St and Marble Hill Avenue on Thursday night and witnessed ICE arresting Oscar Belgal, 28, after he had been shot in the neck, apparently with an assault-style rifle.

Continue reading...
title: New York City’s Marble Hill residents furious after ICE shooting: ‘Why do this?’

author: Shrai Popat in Washington
description:
Zacharia will replace Karoline Leavitt, who left the role at the end of August after giving birth to her second child

Donald Trump has chosen the conservative commentator Katie Zacharia to be the next White House press secretary, according to a White House official.

Zacharia would replace Karoline Leavitt, who left the role at the end of August after the birth to her second child.

Continue reading...
title: Trump picks conservative commentator Katie Zacharia to be next press secretary

author: Guardian staff and agencies
description:
Hazardous waves are possible in Costa Rica, Ecuador, Peru, Nicaragua, Guatemala, El Salvador and Mexico

A powerful 7.6 magnitude earthquake has struck Panama and triggered tsunami warnings along the west coast of Central and South America, according to the US Geological Survey (USGS).

The quake hit along the southern coast of the country, the USGS said. It was centered near the southern tip of the Central American country, about 14km (9 miles) south-west of the remote community of Pitaloza Arriba, the USGS said.

Continue reading...
title: Powerful 7.6-magnitude earthquake hits Panama and triggers tsunami warnings

author: Adam Gabbatt and agencies
description:
Governor halts execution of William Lee Thompson, after Christa Pike survived failed lethal injections

Ron DeSantis cancelled a planned execution in the state on Friday, days before a 74-year-old man was due to be killed by lethal injection.

The move – the first time Florida’s governor has withdrawn a death warrant in his nearly eight years in office – comes just over a week after the botched execution of Christa Pike in Tennessee.

Continue reading...
title: Florida execution called off after DeSantis withdraws death warrant for first time

author: Sammy Gecsoyler and Peter Walker
description:
Party now polling 15 points above Greens, who had been ahead of Labour before Keir Starmer resigned as PM

Labour is starting to win back voters on the left who became disillusioned under Keir Starmer’s leadership, the party’s deputy leader has claimed after it saw off Zack Polanski and the Greens to win the Holborn and St Pancras byelection.

Labour’s Sagal Abdi-Wali took 45% of a relatively low turnout to keep Starmer’s old north London seat for the party, pushing Polanski, who had stood for the party he leads, into second place on 33%.

Continue reading...
title: Labour byelection win shows party starting to win back voters on left

author: Associated Press
description:
Multiple hospitalized after Avianca flight from Medellín to New York had to divert to Miami due to strong turbulence

At least eight people were injured when an Avianca flight encountered severe turbulence and had to make an emergency landing in Miami early on Friday.

Miami-Dade fire rescue said one person was rushed to a trauma center with severe injuries while seven others were taken to area hospitals in ambulances.

Continue reading...
title: Severe turbulence injures at least eight and forces emergency landing in Miami

author: Esther Addley
description:
Decades of volunteering combined with years of active local party politics, propels Abdi-Wali to victory over Green leader Zack Polanski

For Sagal Abdi-Wali, the new MP for Holborn and St Pancras, being elected to replace Keir Starmer in the north London constituency is “deeply personal”, she said in her acceptance speech.

The 43-year-old has lived in the area since the 1990s when, as a seven-year-old, she fled war-torn Somalia with her mother and four brothers, eventually settling in Gospel Oak in Camden, which largely falls within the constituency. Her journey from refugee to member of parliament was one which she hoped would inspire “people who look like me”, she said. “This is Camden and this is Britain.”

Continue reading...
title: ‘The real deal’: Sagal Abdi-Wali’s journey from child refugee to Labour MP in former PM’s seat

author: Ariana Baio in New York
description:
Trump administration says US ‘doesn’t need’ ICC after accusing court of unfairly targeting Americans for war crime charges

The United States was accused of launching “an assault” on the world’s legal order after imposing more sanctions on the international criminal court (ICC).

Unveiling the Trump administration’s latest escalation against the court, which it has accused of politicization and unfairly targeting Americans for war crime charges, Marco Rubio, the US secretary of state, declared: “Either the ICC will end its threats, or we will end the ICC.”

Continue reading...
title: US imposes new sanctions on international criminal court

author: Kevin Rawlinson
description:
Regulator says poll cited by Virginia McVea in move to strip rescue officers of pay did not sufficiently back up her claim

The head of the UK coastguard agency is facing calls to resign after she was found to have used unverified data to back up her controversial plan to strip rescue officers of their pay.

Virginia McVea, the chief executive of the Maritime and Coastguard Agency (MCA), claimed more than 90% of coastguard rescue officers supported the proposal, citing an official survey. Now, after an Office for Statistics Regulation (OSR) investigation, the agency has admitted its poll did not sufficiently back up the claim.

Continue reading...
title: UK coastguard agency chief faces calls to resign over use of unverified data to back up pay plan

author: Gaya Gupta
description:
US president renews his efforts to oust Cook despite supreme court ruling that her firing was unconstitutional

Donald Trump announced on Friday that he is establishing a committee to investigate Lisa Cook, the US Federal Reserve governor, over allegations that she committed mortgage fraud, renewing his efforts to oust her despite a June supreme court ruling that her earlier firing was unconstitutional.

Trump said a committee will consult with justice department officials to decide whether there is “cause” for her removal. The White House will hold an in-person hearing on 5 November to consider the allegations against Cook, which will be closed to the public but transcribed and published. Cook will be able to submit a written statement to present her own evidence and will be subject to examination from White House and her own legal counsel.
title: Trump establishes committee to investigate Fed governor Lisa Cook

author: Joanna Partridge
description:
Former City banker becomes eighth to clear their name, just days after five others were acquitted

Former City trader Christian Bittar has become the eighth person to have his conviction for rigging interest rates quashed, just days after five other former bankers also successfully cleared their names.

Christian Bittar, who previously worked for Deutsche Bank, was convicted in 2018 of conspiracy to defraud.

Continue reading...
title: Christian Bittar has conviction for rigging interest rates quashed

author: Ariana Baio
description:
Dr Annie Andrews voices opposition to ‘biological men ... in women’s sports’ in response to Republican attacks

Dr Annie Andrews, a Democratic Senate candidate in South Carolina, has responded to persistent efforts by Republicans to make trans athletes in women’s sports a wedge issue in the race.

In a restrained direct-to-camera statement, Andrews – a pediatrician – outlined her opposition to “biological men playing in women’s sports”, as her party pushes back against Republican attacks.

Continue reading...
title: Democratic Senate candidate responds to anti-trans attacks pushed by Republicans

author: Nicola Davis Science correspondent
description:
Warning follows Pete Hegseth announcement that firing squad execution of Fort Hood killer will be public

• US politics – latest updates

Livestreaming an execution could cause post-traumatic stress disorder in the viewing public, mental health experts have said, after the US confirmed plans to broadcast the death by firing squad of a man who shot dead 13 unarmed soldiers.

The US defence secretary, Pete Hegseth, said on Thursday that Nidal Hasan, a former army psychiatrist who killed 13 people at Fort Hood in 2009, would be executed by firing squad on 3 December. Officials later confirmed it would be livestreamed. It is believed it will be the first public execution in the
title: Execution live stream could cause PTSD in viewers, say psychiatrists

author: Rowena Mason Whitehall editor
description:
Reform UK shadow chancellor seeks to associate Tory leader with metropolitan elite as party relations sour further

  • UK politics live – latest updates

Robert Jenrick has launched an extended attack on Kemi Badenoch for being part of a metropolitan elite, saying a coalition deal with the Tories would be like being “handcuffed to a zombie”.

The Reform UK shadow chancellor repeatedly called the Tory leader “Kensington Kemi” and claimed her party was for people who moan about the decline of Mayfair clubs and complain that they cannot find Ottolenghi recipe ingredients in the shops.

Continue reading...
title: Robert Jenrick launches scathing broadside against ‘Kensington Kemi’

author: Kalyeena Makortoff Banking correspondent
description:
Exclusive: Chancellor urged to reverse Rishi Sunak’s tax surcharge cuts to claw back billions in lost revenue

  • Business live – latest updates

Tax cuts for big banks have deprived the UK government of £6bn in revenues, according to campaigners, who are calling on the chancellor, John Healey, to increase taxes and force lenders to pay their “fair share” in the upcoming budget.

Calculations by the Trades Union Congress (TUC), which represents unions with more than 5.3 million members across England and Wales, shows that the public purse is billions of pounds worse off as a result of tax cuts introduced under the Tory chancellor Rishi Sunak in 2023.

Continue reading...
title: Tory tax break for banks has cost UK public purse £6bn, says TUC

author: Lex McMenamin and Joanna Walters in New York
description:
US immigration officer shot man in car where five-year-old child was sitting in the Bronx, sparking fierce protests

  • US politics live – latest updates

Leading New York Democrats expressed anger and demanded curbs on Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) violence after a federal officer shot a man in a car where a five-year-old child was sitting, sparking fierce protests.

At least seven shots were reportedly fired and the man was hit in the neck late afternoon on Thursday as children were coming home from school in the busy Marble Hill neighborhood of the south Bronx in New York City.
title: ‘Abolish ICE’: Mamdani, AOC and other Democrats urge action after New York shooting

author: Marina Dunbar
description:
Fight in East Fishkill, New York, part of a growing divide over whether AI benefits outweigh enormous downsides

For decades, East Fishkill helped build New York’s tech industry.

The hamlet, located 70 miles north of New York City, was home to a 460-acre campus where IBM researched and manufactured semiconductor chips for nearly fifty years.

Continue reading...
title: ‘This is not an anti-tech town’: backlash to datacenter in city once home to IBM

author: Pjotr Sauer
description:
Founder of influential Rybar blog detained after warnings of attempts to destabilise Balkan country, officials say

A leading pro-Kremlin Russian military blogger with reported ties to Russia’s intelligence services has been arrested in Montenegro, after warnings of attempts to destabilise the Balkan country, officials have said.

Mikhail Zvinchuk, the founder of the influential Rybar war blog, was detained on Friday alongside his wife and three other Russians by police and security agents in the Adriatic resort town of Risan, on suspicion of spreading Russian influence, local media reported.

Continue reading...
title: Pro-Kremlin Russian military blogger Mikhail Zvinchuk arrested in Montenegro

author: Sarah Butler
description:
Online retailer’s 26% jump sharpens focus on exemption letting cheap parcels into the country duty-free

Shein, the online fast-fashion retailer founded in China, increased sales in the UK by just over a quarter last year, overtaking British rival Asos.

The company, whose global parent group listed on the Hong Kong stock exchange and valued at just over $26bn (£19.6bn) last month, increased sales at its UK division by 26% to £2.58bn, according to accounts filed at Companies House.

Continue reading...
title: Shein outsells British rival Asos as UK revenue hits £2.58bn

author: Jamie Grierson
description:
Former prince surrendered lease on home within its first 25 years after public outcry about the rent he paid

Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor has been granted £302,000 in compensation after the lease on his former Royal Lodge home in Windsor was officially surrendered.

A crown estate spokesperson said the former prince paid £1.8m in repair and restoration costs, and the lease was handed back more than 50 years early.

Continue reading...
title: Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor granted £302,000 for end of Royal Lodge lease

author: Martin Belam
description:
US president says US will not attack Iran before midterms, while defense secretary says Nidal Hasan will face a firing squad next month. Plus, Sofia Coppola looks back on her glittering directorial career

Good morning. The defense secretary, Pete Hegseth, has said the execution of Nidal Hasan by firing squad will be livestreamed next month, in a radical departure from the previous norm. Hegseth said: “We’ll make sure that people are able to watch it, that it’s public, because people need to understand there’s serious consequences for these types of things.”

Hasan opened fire at a medical processing center at Fort Hood, Texas, on 5 November 2009, killing 13 people and wounding dozens more. A military jury sentenced him to death in 2013 and he has been held at Fort Leavenworth in Kansas ever since. The last known case of a military firing squad in the US was in Novembe
title: Hegseth promises execution live stream as Trump appears to ‘pause’ war on Iran | First Thing

author: Guardian staff and agencies in Oslo
description:
Norwegian committee recognises achievements of former UN rights chief who stood up against apartheid in South Africa

  • Nobel peace prize – latest updates

Former UN human rights chief Navanethem “Navi” Pillay, a judge on the international court of justice (ICJ), has won the Nobel peace prize.

Pillay, 85, from South Africa, who is a judge with the international court of justice, was recognised for her efforts to promote peace and international law, said Jørgen Watne Frydnes, chair of the Norwegian Nobel committee.

Continue reading...
title: ICJ judge Navi Pillay wins Nobel peace prize for promoting international law

author: Kiran Stacey Policy editor
description:
Exclusive: Abena Oppong-Asare urges chancellor to unlock billions of pounds, as housing associations say they could build 41,000 homes in 10 years

The Labour chair of the Commons housing committee is urging John Healey to bring forward billions of pounds of planned spending on social and affordable homes in England, after housing associations said they were ready to build tens of thousands more.

Abena Oppong-Asare called for the chancellor to allocate money from the £39bn Social and Affordable Homes Programme (SAHP) as soon as possible, rather than after the election as planned.

Continue reading...
title: Labour chair of housing committee calls for urgent funds for affordable homes in England

author: Jakub Krupa
description:
The winner will be announced in a ceremony that starts at 10am UK time (11am CEST)

Last year’s peace prize was won by Venezuelan politician María Corina Machado for her dogged struggle to rescue the South American country from its fate as “a brutal, authoritarian state”.

She later presented her award to Donald Trump, meeting him in the White House, nearly a fortnight after he ordered the abduction of Venezuela’s president, Nicolás Maduro.

Continue reading...
title: Winner of 2026 Nobel peace prize to be announced - Europe live

author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
description:
It may sound odd to think Zack Polanski would be happy with second place, but after the most challenging week of his political life it could have been worse

  • Holborn and St Pancras byelection – live updates

  • Labour’s Abdi-Wali fends off Polanski and Green party to win byelection

Parliamentary byelections can generate all sorts of emotional responses, often very strong ones. But for the main contenders in Holborn and St Pancras, the feeling this morning might be more prosaic: relief.

For Labour,
title: Holborn and St Pancras byelection loss will disappoint Greens – but there may also be relief

author: Australian Associated Press
description:
Global sportswear brand is suing online retailer in the federal court for selling clothes featuring ‘deceptively similar’ design

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Global sportswear brand Adidas claims Australian label White Fox is trying to trade off its reputation by infringing its distinctive three-stripe trademark.

Adidas is suing the online fast-fashion retailer in the Federal Court for selling clothes with a four-stripe design, which it argues is deceptively similar to its classic design.

Continue reading...
title: Adidas accuses Australian label White Fox of ‘trading off its reputation’ with use of four-stripe branding

author: Nino Bucci Courts and justice reporter
description:
Employee had also been in Bali when he told his manager he was working from home, Fair Work Commission hears

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A Sydney currency trader who was sacked for working from Singapore without approval has won an unfair dismissal case, but failed to be awarded compensation.

The Fair Work Commission ruled on Wednesday that Charles Graham had been unfairly dismissed by HIFX Australia, trading as Xe, in December last year.

Continue reading...
title: Sydney trader sacked for working from Singapore without permission wins unfair dismissal case

author: Rachel Salvidge
description:
Exclusive: Firms made more than £340m last year from processing industrial and commercial wastewater at sewage works that are unable to remove many chemical pollutants

Water companies in the UK made more than £340m in revenue last year by pouring billions of litres of industrial and commercial wastewater into sewage treatment works that experts say are not designed to remove most chemicals, leaving pollutants to pass into rivers, seas and farmland.

Water companies are required by law to take industrial wastewater and issue permits called “trade-effluent consents” that allow businesses to send it to sewage works, though water companies can refuse applications.

Continue reading...
title: Revealed: the ‘black box’ wastewater trade that rakes in millions for UK utility companies

author: Denis Campbell
description:
Decision by Royal College of Pharmacy to end sponsorship comes after concerns over Teva Pharmaceuticals’ ‘activities’

A second major UK health body has cut ties with an Israeli drug firm after coming under pressure from pro-Palestine campaigners.

The Royal College of Pharmacy has dropped Teva UK, the British arm of the global medicines producer Teva Pharmaceuticals, as a sponsor of and exhibitor at its annual conference next month.

Continue reading...
title: Second UK health body drops Israeli drug firm after activist pressure

author: Guardian staff and agencies
description:
Saudi Arabia has not commented on claims, but confirmed three killed in airport strikes earlier this week

Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis say they have struck Saudi Arabia’s Riyadh ⁠airport with a ballistic missile, badly damaging a plane and leading some airlines to suspend flights to the capital.

The group provided no evidence, and Saudi Arabia did not immediately comment on the claim.

Continue reading...
title: Houthis claim attack on Riyadh airport as airlines suspend flights to Saudi capital

author: Adam Fulton
description:
Results are expected from 2.30am BST in the north London poll to choose a replacement for former PM Keir Starmer

A quick reminder of the byelection candidates in Holborn and St Pancras:

Labour – Sagal Abdi-Wali

Green party – Zack Polanski

Conservative party – Ewan Cameron

Rejoin EU – Briony Anne Lonbay Kapoor

UK Voice – Ketankumar Pipaliya

Ukip – Ben Walker

Monster Raving Loony party – Barmy Brunch

Com
title: Counting under way in Holborn and St Pancras byelection – UK politics live

author: Dee Jefferson
description:
Making its southern hemisphere debut, Dance Reflections will feature collaborators of Rosalía, Madonna and Beyoncé – and a high-wire takeover of the Cutaway

  • Get our weekend culture and lifestyle email

A “once-in-a-lifetime” program of dance works of scale will be coming to Sydney in January, including 11 international works from France, Belgium, South Africa and beyond making their Australian premiere.

The program, which triples the scale of the dance offering at the last Sydney festival, will bring 174 performers and crew to Sydney, with the crowning jewel being the acclaimed French choreographer Rachid Ouramdane’s Outsider. The 2024 work features 21 dancers from the Ballet du Grand Théâtre de Genève and four elite athletes, navigating a “cat’s cradle” of high wires and slack line
title: Sydney festival 2027: 11 international dance works to headline ‘once-in-a-lifetime’ program

author: Tess Ikonomou
description:
Treasurer earmarks funds for year-long transition period for tax office, delaying ban’s 30 November start date

A controversial credit card ban for payments on tax bills will be delayed by six months as extra funding is announced for the Australian Tax Office.

Treasurer Jim Chalmers announced on Friday extra funding for the ATO to halt the change until the end of June.

Continue reading...
title: Jim Chalmers delays ATO’s controversial ban on credit card payments following business outcry
